text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Opposition leaders and the National Convention Executive Council pro-reform alliance agree to present their agenda for constitutional reforms to President Daniel arap Moi on Wednesday.
- The government is to investigate allegations a businessman supplied supplied Nairobi City Council with chalk instead of chlorine for 70 million shillings.
- At least 70 foreigners are arrested in Nairobi on Monday night, a few hours after President Moi said foreign spies and criminals masquerading as refugees had invaded the city.
- Opposition leaders opposed to meeting Moi for talks on reforms are urged to subdue their personal ambitions for the sake of Kenya's long-term interests.
- A six-year old Ugandan boy is rescued from alleged torture and confinement by his aunt in western Kenya.
- Business in the towns of Thika and Karatina towns in central Kenya is paralysed for a day after rival minibus operators clash.
- A meeting by opposition coalition parties to select delegates to discuss constitutional reforms with President Moi fails to agree on the basis of selection.
- The government deploys security forces to flush out cattle rustlers who invaded a shopping centre in Garissa for a fourth straight day. ($1=59 Kenyan Shillings)
